q: Matter is used to cover all the substances and materials from which the _____ is composed.
e: Matter is used to cover all the substances and materials from which the physical universe is composed. Physical universe is the idea that completes this fact. Chemical universe would fill a different blank than physical universe.

q: Nowadays, there is a fourth state of matter known as _____ which is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles.
e: Nowadays, there is a fourth state of matter known as plasma which is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles. Plasma is the idea that completes this fact. Colloid would fill a different blank than plasma.

q: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with _____ forces between one another.
e: The particles in a solid are packed very tightly together with strong forces between one another. In a solid, particles are packed tightly with strong forces, so the shape is fixed. Moderate would fill a different blank than strong.

q: Solids have a definite _____ and volume.
e: Solids have a definite shape and volume. Shape is the idea that completes this fact. Mass would fill a different blank than shape.

q: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together _____ than those in gases.
e: Liquids can have a definite volume, because the particles in liquid are held together more strongly than those in gases. More strongly is the idea that completes this fact. More weakly would fill a different blank than more strongly.

q: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of _____ attractive forces between gaseous particles.
e: The particles in a gas are in constant and rapid motion because of weak attractive forces between gaseous particles. In a gas, particles are far apart, move fast, and have weak attractions. Strong would fill a different blank than weak.

q: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from _____ with the gas or liquid particles.
e: Brownian motion is the continuous random movement of small particles suspended in a gas or liquid, which arises from collisions with the gas or liquid particles. Collisions is the idea that completes this fact. Attractions would fill a different blank than collisions.

q: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of _____ substance.
e: In diffusion, the particles of one substance mix with and move through the particles of another substance. Another is the idea that completes this fact. A solid would fill a different blank than another.

q: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the _____.
e: The speed of diffusion of particles is affected by the mass of particles and by the temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact. Volume would fill a different blank than temperature.

q: The bigger the mass, the _____ the particles diffuse.
e: The bigger the mass, the slower the particles diffuse. Slower is the idea that completes this fact. Faster would fill a different blank than slower.

q: The smaller the mass, the _____ the particles diffuse.
e: The smaller the mass, the faster the particles diffuse. Faster is the idea that completes this fact. Steadier would fill a different blank than faster.

q: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse _____.
e: The higher the temperature, it enables the particles to diffuse faster. Faster is the idea that completes this fact. Randomly would fill a different blank than faster.

q: Unlike gases, solids cannot be compressed and do not _____.
e: Unlike gases, solids cannot be compressed and do not flow. Flow is the idea that completes this fact. Vibrate is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Solids do expand _____ when heated.
e: Solids do expand slightly when heated. Slightly is the idea that completes this fact. Rapidly would fill a different blank than slightly.

q: Liquids can take up the shape of the container because particles are able to move _____ throughout the liquids.
e: Liquids can take up the shape of the container because particles are able to move freely throughout the liquids. Freely is the idea that completes this fact. Slowly would fill a different blank than freely.

q: The gas in a container spreads out to occupy the whole space of the container taking its shape and _____.
e: The gas in a container spreads out to occupy the whole space of the container taking its shape and volume. Volume is the idea that completes this fact. Density would fill a different blank than volume.

q: Diffusion is mainly seen in _____ and gases.
e: Diffusion is mainly seen in liquids and gases. Liquids is the idea that completes this fact. Plasmas would fill a different blank than liquids.

q: Plasma is a hot _____ gas containing charged particles.
e: Plasma is a hot ionised gas containing charged particles. Ionised is the idea that completes this fact. Magnetic would fill a different blank than ionised.

q: When a few drops of perfume are released into a room, the particles of perfume move through the air and _____ the room.
e: When a few drops of perfume are released into a room, the particles of perfume move through the air and spread the room. Spread is the idea that completes this fact. Cool would fill a different blank than spread.

q: Preparing tea using a tea bag in hot water is an example of _____ in daily life.
e: Preparing tea using a tea bag in hot water is an example of diffusion in daily life. Diffusion is the spreading of particles from higher to lower concentration. Filtration would fill a different blank than diffusion.

q: The motion of pollen grains on still water is an example of _____ motion.
e: The motion of pollen grains on still water is an example of Brownian motion. Brownian motion is the random jiggling of tiny particles hit by fast molecules in a fluid. Rotary would fill a different blank than Brownian.

q: Mercury and bromine are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Mercury and bromine are examples of elements that are liquids at room temperature. Liquids is the idea that completes this fact. Gases would fill a different blank than liquids.

q: Oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and chlorine are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and chlorine are examples of elements that are gases at room temperature. Gases is the idea that completes this fact. Solids would fill a different blank than gases.

q: Copper, iron, zinc, silver, gold, carbon and phosphorus are examples of elements that are _____ at room temperature.
e: Copper, iron, zinc, silver, gold, carbon and phosphorus are examples of elements that are solids at room temperature. Solids is the idea that completes this fact. Liquids would fill a different blank than solids.

q: Metals have _____ density compared to non-metals.
e: Metals have high density compared to non-metals. High is the idea that completes this fact. Low would fill a different blank than high.
